'''John Holmes Malmberg''' (July 5, 1927 – November 17, 1992) was an American plasma [[physicist]] and a professor at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name=":0" /> He was known for making the first experimental measurements of [[Landau damping]] of [[plasma waves]] in 1964,<ref name=":1" /> as well as for his research on [[non-neutral plasmas]] and the development of the [[Penning–Malmberg trap]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

In 1985, Malmberg won the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for his experimental work on wave-particle interactions in neutral plasmas and his studies on pure electron plasmas.<ref name=":4" /> He was later co-awarded the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] in 1991 for his contribution to research on [[non-neutral plasmas]].<ref name=":5" />

== Early life and career ==
Malmberg studied at [[Illinois State University]] (bachelor 1949) and the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] (master 1951), where he received his doctorate in 1957. From 1957 to 1969, he was a staff scientist working in the area of plasma physics at [[General Atomics]] in [[San Diego, California]]. From 1967 until his death, he was a professor of physics at the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD) in [[La Jolla, California]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-11-24-me-914-story.html|title=Plasma Physics Pioneer at UCSD Dies|date=1992-11-24|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11606003.html|title=Malmberg, J. H.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref>

In 1980, Malmberg was appointed to the first Plasma Sciences Committee of the [[National Research Council (United States)|National Research Council]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2020}} In that capacity, he was a strong voice for the importance of basic plasma experiments in maintaining the health of plasma science. In an era when small-scale and basic plasma physics research was nearing an ebb, Malmberg emphasized the importance of being able to follow the internal logic of the science, which he believed to be of paramount importance in doing basic research.

== Scientific contributions ==

=== Landau damping of plasma waves ===
Malmberg and Charles Wharton made the first experimental measurements of [[Landau damping]] of [[plasma waves]] in 1964,<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Malmberg|first1=J. H.|last2=Wharton|first2=C. B.|date=1964|title=Collisionless Damping of Electrostatic Plasma Waves|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=13|issue=6|pages=184–186|bibcode=1964PhRvL..13..184M|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184}}</ref> two decades after its prediction by [[Lev Landau]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Landau|first=L. D.|title=On the vibrations of the electronic plasma|journal=Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz.|volume=16|pages=574–86 (reprinted 1965 Collected Papers of Landau ed D ter Haar (Oxford: Pergamon) pp 445–60)}}</ref> Since this damping is collisionless, the [[Free energy (thermodynamics)|free energy]] and [[Phase space|phase-space]] memory associated with the damped wave are not lost, but are subtly stored in the plasma. Malmberg and collaborators demonstrated explicitly the [[Reversible process (thermodynamics)|reversible nature of this process]] by observation of the plasma wave echo<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.219|title = Plasma Wave Echo|year = 1967|last1 = Gould|first1 = R. W.|last2 = O'Neil|first2 = T. M.|last3 = Malmberg|first3 = J. H.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 19|issue = 5|pages = 219–222|bibcode = 1967PhRvL..19..219G| url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/1683/ |url-access = subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1063/1.1692075|title = Observation of Plasma Wave Echoes|year = 1968|last1 = Malmberg|first1 = J. H.|last2 = Wharton|first2 = C. B.|last3 = Gould|first3 = R. W.|last4 = O'Neil|first4 = T. M.|journal = Physics of Fluids|volume = 11|issue = 6|page = 1147|bibcode = 1968PhFl...11.1147M|url = https://authors.library.caltech.edu/6114/1/MALpof68.pdf}}</ref> in which a wave "spontaneously" appears in the plasma as an 'echo' of two previously launched waves that had been Landau damped. 

=== Penning–Malmberg traps and non-neutral plasmas ===
{{see also|Penning–Malmberg trap}}
Neutral plasmas are notoriously difficult to confine. In contrast, Malmberg and collaborators predicted and demonstrated experimentally<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.577|title = Properties of Nonneutral Plasma|year = 1975|last1 = Malmberg|first1 = J. H.|last2 = Degrassie|first2 = J. S.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 35|issue = 9|pages = 577–580|bibcode = 1975PhRvL..35..577M}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.44.654|title = Long-Time Containment of a Pure Electron Plasma|year = 1980|last1 = Malmberg|first1 = J. H.|last2 = Driscoll|first2 = C. F.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 44|issue = 10|pages = 654–657|bibcode = 1980PhRvL..44..654M}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1063/1.862904|title = A confinement theorem for nonneutral plasmas|year = 1980|last1 = o'Neil|first1 = T. M.|journal = Physics of Fluids|volume = 23|issue = 11|page = 2216|bibcode = 1980PhFl...23.2216O}}</ref> that plasmas with a single sign of charge, such as pure [[electron]] or pure ion plasmas, can be confined for long periods (e.g., hours). This was accomplished using an arrangement of electric and magnetic fields similar to that of a [[Penning trap]], but optimized to confine single-component plasmas. In recognition of Malmberg's contributions to the development of these devices, they are now referred to as [[Penning–Malmberg trap|Penning–Malmberg traps]]. 

Malmberg and collaborators, realized that [[non-neutral plasmas]] offer research opportunities not available with neutral plasmas. In contrast to neutral plasmas, plasmas with a single sign of charge can reach states of global thermal equilibria.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1063/1.862578|title = Finite length thermal equilibria of a pure electron plasma column|year = 1979|last1 = Prasad|first1 = S. A.|last2 = o'Neil|first2 = T. M.|journal = Physics of Fluids|volume = 22|issue = 2|page = 278|bibcode = 1979PhFl...22..278P}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.1290|title = Observation of transport to thermal equilibrium in pure electron plasmas|year = 1988|last1 = Driscoll|first1 = C. F.|last2 = Malmberg|first2 = J. H.|last3 = Fine|first3 = K. S.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 60|issue = 13|pages = 1290–1293|pmid = 10037997|bibcode = 1988PhRvL..60.1290D}}</ref> The possibility of using thermal equilibrium [[statistical mechanics]] to describe the plasma provides a large advantage to theory.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/RevModPhys.71.87|title = Trapped nonneutral plasmas, liquids, and crystals (The thermal equilibrium states)|year = 1999|last1 = Dubin|first1 = Daniel H. E.|last2 = o'Neil|first2 = T. M.|journal = Reviews of Modern Physics|volume = 71|issue = 1|pages = 87–172|bibcode = 1999RvMP...71...87D}}</ref> Furthermore, states near such thermal equilibria can be more easily controlled experimentally and departures from equilibrium studied with precision.  

When a neutral plasma is cooled, it simply [[Recombine (physics)|recombines]]; but a plasma with a single sign of charge can be cooled without recombination. Malmberg constructed a trap for a pure electron plasma with walls at 4.2 K. [[Cyclotron radiation]] from the electrons then cooled the plasma to a few Kelvin. Theory argued that electron-electron collisions in such a strongly magnetized and low temperature plasma would be qualitatively different than those in warmer plasmas. Malmberg measured the [[Equipartition theorem|equipartition]] rate between electron velocity components parallel to and perpendicular to the magnetic field and confirmed the striking prediction that it decreases exponentially with decreasing temperature.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.317|title = Measurement of collisional anisotropic temperature relaxation in a strongly magnetized pure electron plasma|year = 1992|last1 = Beck|first1 = B. R.|last2 = Fajans|first2 = J.|last3 = Malmberg|first3 = J. H.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 68|issue = 3|pages = 317–320|pmid = 10045861|bibcode = 1992PhRvL..68..317B}}</ref>

Malmberg and [[Thomas Michael O'Neil|Thomas M. O'Neil]] predicted that a very cold, single-species plasma would undergo a [[phase transition]] to a [[Body centered cubic|body-centered cubic]] crystalline state.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.39.1333|title = Pure Electron Plasma, Liquid, and Crystal|year = 1977|last1 = Malmberg|first1 = J. H.|last2 = O'Neil|first2 = T. M.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 39|issue = 21|pages = 1333–1336|bibcode = 1977PhRvL..39.1333M}}</ref> Later, John Bollinger and collaborators created such a state by [[laser cooling]] a plasma of singly ionized [[beryllium]] ions to temperatures of a few millikelvin.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1063/1.873818|title = Crystalline order in laser-cooled, non-neutral ion plasmas|year = 2000|last1 = Bollinger|first1 = J. J.|last2 = Mitchell|first2 = T. B.|last3 = Huang|first3 = X.-P.|last4 = Itano|first4 = W. M.|last5 = Tan|first5 = J. N.|last6 = Jelenković|first6 = B. M.|last7 = Wineland|first7 = D. J.|journal = Physics of Plasmas|volume = 7|issue = 1|pages = 7–13|bibcode = 2000PhPl....7....7B}}</ref>  In other experiments, trapped pure electron plasmas are used to model the two-dimensional (2D) [[vortex dynamics]] expected for an ideal fluid.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.588|title = Measurements of symmetric vortex merger|year = 1991|last1 = Fine|first1 = K. S.|last2 = Driscoll|first2 = C. F.|last3 = Malmberg|first3 = J. H.|last4 = Mitchell|first4 = T. B.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 67|issue = 5|pages = 588–591|pmid = 10044936|bibcode = 1991PhRvL..67..588F}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.3277|title = Relaxation of 2D Turbulence to Vortex Crystals|year = 1995|last1 = Fine|first1 = K. S.|last2 = Cass|first2 = A. C.|last3 = Flynn|first3 = W. G.|last4 = Driscoll|first4 = C. F.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 75|issue = 18|pages = 3277–3280|pmid = 10059543|bibcode = 1995PhRvL..75.3277F}}</ref>

In the late 1980s, pure [[positron]] (i.e., antielectron) plasmas were created using the Penning–Malmberg trap technology.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.62.901|title = Positron Plasma in the Laboratory|year = 1989|last1 = Surko|first1 = C. M.|last2 = Leventhal|first2 = M.|last3 = Passner|first3 = A.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 62|issue = 8|pages = 901–904|pmid = 10040367|bibcode = 1989PhRvL..62..901S}}</ref> This, and advances in confining low-energy [[Antiproton|antiprotons]],<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2504|title = First Capture of Antiprotons in a Penning Trap: A Kiloelectronvolt Source|year = 1986|last1 = Gabrielse|first1 = G.|last2 = Fei|first2 = X.|last3 = Helmerson|first3 = K.|last4 = Rolston|first4 = S. L.|last5 = Tjoelker|first5 = R.|last6 = Trainor|first6 = T. A.|last7 = Kalinowsky|first7 = H.|last8 = Haas|first8 = J.|last9 = Kells|first9 = W.|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 57|issue = 20|pages = 2504–2507|pmid = 10033784|bibcode = 1986PhRvL..57.2504G|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/679960|url-access = subscription}}</ref> led to the creation of low-energy [[antihydrogen]] a decade later.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1038/nature01096|title = Production and detection of cold antihydrogen atoms|year = 2002|last1 = Amoretti|first1 = M.|last2 = Amsler|first2 = C.|last3 = Bonomi|first3 = G.|last4 = Bouchta|first4 = A.|last5 = Bowe|first5 = P.|last6 = Carraro|first6 = C.|last7 = Cesar|first7 = C. Malmberg's studies with trapped single-component and non-neutral plasmas were important in shaping the development of subsequent sub-fields of plasma physics with broad impacts in the wider world of physics.

== Honors and awards ==
In 1985, Malmberg received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]] for "''his outstanding experimental studies which expanded our understanding of wave-particle interactions in neutral plasmas and increased our confidence in plasma theory; and for his pioneering studies of the confinement and transport of pure electron plasmas''".<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Malmberg&first_nm=John&year=1985|title=1985 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref>   

And in 1991, he was co-awarded the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] with Charles F. Driscoll and [[Thomas Michael O'Neil|Thomas M. O'Neil]], for their studies of single-component electron plasmas.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/dawson.cfm|title=John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref>  There is a video, filmed in 1987, where Malmberg and [[Thomas Michael O'Neil|Tom O'Neil]] describe their research.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Malmberg |first1=John H |last2=O'Neil |first2=Thomas M |title=Pure electron plasmas near thermal equilibrium (1987) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zqRmxi9GQWs |website=YouTube |access-date=7 May 2026}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
In 1993, the UCSD physics department established the John Holmes Malmberg Prize in his honor. It is awarded annually to an outstanding undergraduate physics major with interests in experimental physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www-physics.ucsd.edu/Awards|title=UC San Diego {{!}} Fellowships and Awards in Physics|website=www-physics.ucsd.edu|access-date=2020-02-23}}</ref>
